year.label: Copa Fusca, Brazilian Beetle one-make racing

identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian-built Volkswagen Beetle, known locally as the Fusca, raced as a one-make category. It keeps the air-cooled Beetle's rear transaxle with four forward gears.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. No automatic cut or blip was present, so the driver supplies the upshift lift.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.copa-fusca.20260814t042724969z-bc50b201 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the Beetle transaxle and the exact simulator identity was observed live.
The source describes the transaxle gears as constant-mesh with balk ring synchronisers and places synchronisers on all four forward gears; the live drive selected four H-pattern gears.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.

driver_summary: The Beetle transaxle is constant-mesh with balk-ring synchronisers on all four forward gears, so the blip eases the synchros but the gear engages without it.
